Exempt a figure's overlay axes from the shared styling

Source: R/plot_marginals.R
mark_overlay_axes.Rd

Marks axes as belonging to panels drawn beside the main plot, such as marginal distributions, annotation strips, or gene tracks. apply_uniform_styling() then leaves them as they were drawn: the Axes tab's fonts, ticks, gridlines, and lines are not applied to them, reference lines are not drawn on them, and they do not count as facets, so the plot's own axis titles stay draggable. This is the approach for a figure built with hand-set axis domains, where only the primary xaxis and yaxis follow the Axes tab.

Usage

mark_overlay_axes(fig, axes)

Arguments

fig

A plotly figure, already built with plotly::plotly_build().

axes

Character vector of layout axis names ("xaxis2", "yaxis3"), not trace references ("x2", "y3").

Value

The figure, with axes added to any axes already marked.

Details

Link an overlay panel to the plot with matches, as add_marginal_plots() does, so it zooms and pans with it.

See also

add_marginal_plots(), apply_uniform_styling()

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

fig <- plotly::plot_ly()
fig <- plotly::add_trace(fig, x = 1:3, y = 1:3, type = "scatter", mode = "lines")
fig <- plotly::add_trace(fig,
    x = 1:3, y = 3:1, type = "scatter", mode = "lines", xaxis = "x2", yaxis = "y2"
)
fig <- plotly::layout(fig,
    xaxis = list(domain = c(0, 1)), yaxis = list(domain = c(0, 0.8)),
    xaxis2 = list(domain = c(0, 1), matches = "x", anchor = "y2"),
    yaxis2 = list(domain = c(0.85, 1))
)
fig <- plotly::plotly_build(fig)
mark_overlay_axes(fig, c("xaxis2", "yaxis2"))
